facts.label: Starship Flight 16
facts.summary: December 2026 target, reported. FAA CADENA air-traffic planning slides (22 Oct) list Flight 16 NET 10 Dec 2026, as the first flight from Florida (LC-39A). NASASpaceflight (25 Oct) estimates the first LC-39A Starship flight could be in late January 2027. This is reporting, not a SpaceX date.

facts.label: Starship Flight 15
facts.source: FAA CADENA planning deck, 29 Oct 2026, Upcoming High-Profile Missions slide: Starship FLT-15 NOV 12 (https://compass.atfm.aero/public_svcdynamic/getfile?download=false&fileuuid=0fb6079b-6d10-4039-8766-b3ccb3c877f0)
facts.summary: NET 12 November on the FAA's 29 Oct 2026 air-traffic planning slides (moved from 8 Nov), not a SpaceX T-0. On the 20 Oct earnings call Musk said SpaceX expects Flight 15 next month and will try to catch both the booster and the ship. Booster 22 completed a full-duration 33-engine static fire on 25 Oct, per SpaceX. NASASpaceflight and Next Spaceflight report a Ship 42 single-engine static fire at Massey’s on 26 Oct, then a six-engine, roughly 60-second full-duration fire on 27 Oct 2026, about 4:46pm CDT (about 21:46 Irish time). SpaceX hasn’t posted about the Ship 42 fires. Both Flight 15 vehicles have now static-fired. Still no FAA licence and no SpaceX date.
